subject: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation

Hi Asha 

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Call recap
- Primary objective: improve intent classification and slot extraction for in-store returns flow (high precision for fraud risk signals).
- Current infra: RetailCo uses an internal ranking+NLP pipeline with a light LLM layer for edge-case responses.
- Main risk: recent model rollout at RetailCo caused a ~6% drop in golden-set F1 on the returns prompts you shared.

Recommended model candidates (based on your latency and budget targets)
- Llama2-13B-chat (Redwood-optimized)  good balance of cost & accuracy for instruction-style prompts
- Mistral-Instruct-8B  lower cost, strong on concision/slot extraction with careful prompt engineering
- RedModel-7B-q4 (quantized)  for tight latency SLOs on Dedicated instances

What we'll do next (proposed)
1) Share a reproducible eval prompt set (attached: eval_prompt_set_v1.json) and baseline benchmark (eval_report_v1.pdf).
2) Run a controlled A/B: current production model vs recommended candidate(s) on your golden set + sampled live traffic (1M tokens).
3) If we observe regression after our internal model updates, we will produce a diff report and propose either pinning to the previous serving model or a rollback plan.
4) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next Wed to review A/B results and rollout options.

Attachments: eval_prompt_set_v1.json, eval_report_v1.pdf
Drive folder with full evals: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-evals
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890

Next steps (action items)
- Asha: confirm access to the Drive folder or share a preferred S3 location.
- Marissa: run initial candidate benchmark by next Tuesday and share results.
- Dev: readiness to reproduce the regression and prepare a pin/rollback playbook.

Talk soon 

 Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@retailco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: RetailCo ML Team <ml-team@retailco.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation

Hey Marissa 

Thanks for the detailed recap and the files  I was able to download eval_prompt_set_v1.json. Granting the team Drive access now.

A couple of clarifications from our side:
- The regression we observed was after our vendor pushed model version v20261030 to production (not an infrastructure change). The F1 drop was concentrated on the "reason_for_return" slot and an upstream reranker score shift.
- We absolutely want to run an A/B. Our procurement team will need a quick note on rollback procedures and any SLA impacts if we pin older versions.

Can your team reproduce the delta on our golden set, or do you need a traffic capture snippet? Also, curious if your recommended candidates include any pinned-version strategy for the short term.

Asha
Director of ML, RetailCo
asha.patel@retailco.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation

Hi Asha 

Quick answer: we can reproduce a similar drop on the golden set after running the same prompts against the v20261030 artifact. Dev added notes below and we'll run a full A/B this week.

Short-term mitigation options
- Pin to v20261001 (previous artifact) for the affected routes while we triage. Pinning is the fastest way to regain baseline behavior; it can be scoped per-route in Redwood Dedicated/Private so other routes can use newer model variants.
- Canary rollout with fail-open fallback to v20261001 for sessions that hit the bad behavioral signals.
- If pinning isn't acceptable, we can prepare a rollback playbook and estimate SLA window impact (expected < 15 min for a controlled rollback on Dedicated infra; Hosted API requires coordination with support and an agreed maintenance window).

Attachments: eval_report_v2.pdf (initial A/B results  see summary table on page 2).

I'll schedule the 30-min review for next Wed (2026-11-18 10:00 PT)  feel free to propose another time. Dev, can you confirm we have a diff artifact and initial root-cause notes?

 Marissa

On Thu, Nov 12, 2026 at 15:32, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai> wrote:
> From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
> To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
> Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:32:00 -0800
> Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation
>
> Quick tech notes (reproduced locally):
> - Running eval_prompt_set_v1.json against v20261030 shows a 5.8% drop in slot F1 for "reason_for_return" compared to v20261001. Regression appears correlated with a change in tokenizer normalization and a small LM head weight update in the artifact.
> - Generated example (v20261001 -> correct): 
>   "User: I returned this because the item was damaged upon pickup" -> predicted slot: "reason_for_return" = "damaged"
>   (v20261030 -> wrong): predicted slot = "other"
> - We have a candidate diff patch isolating the weight update; running targeted ablations now.
>
> Actionable: we can pin route to v20261001 within the hour once Marissa gives the OK. I will prepare the rollback playbook (steps + monitoring checklist + DocuSign change approval link if needed).
>
> - Dev

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: regression repro notes & pin recommendation

Marissa / Lukas 

Summary of repro (internal)
- Confirmed: v20261030 shows regression on RetailCo golden set (local run).
- Root cause (prelim): tokenizer normalization change + LM head small weight delta in artifact build.
- Workaround: pin affected routes to v20261001. Pinning approach: 
  1) Create a route-level override in the routing policy for the returns flow (returns/*).
  2) Set traffic split: 100% -> v20261001 for 24 hours, monitor rollout metrics for F1, latency, token cost.
  3) If green, extend pin and schedule a staged rollout of the patched artifact.

Attachments for ops: eval_report_v1.pdf, eval_report_v2.pdf
Related links: https://app.redwood.ai/evals/RC-2026-042, DocuSign approval: https://docusign.net/some/approval/rc-042

I can implement the pin once Marissa confirms we have customer approval. Planning note: this requires a short maintenance note to RetailCo procurement with expected SLA impact (<15 min).

- Dev

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Asha Patel <asha.patel@retailco.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.ai>, RetailCo ML Team <ml-team@retailco.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: model fit, evals & regression mitigation

Hi Asha 

Quick update and next steps based on our internal triage: 
- We reproduced the regression and have a recommended short-term mitigation: pin returns routes to v20261001. This is a route-level pin and should be invisible to other workloads.
- Dev will run the pin and monitor for 24 hours. Estimated maintenance window: 10 minutes; no significant SLA exposure expected.
- I've attached the two PDF summaries (eval_report_v1.pdf, eval_report_v2.pdf) and placed the full runs in the Drive folder.

Please reply with a short approval (you can reply "Approve: pin to v20261001") and we'll execute within the next business hour. If you prefer a rollback schedule instead, we can prepare the rollback with DocuSign approval  that will take a bit longer.

Meeting: still on for Wed 2026-11-18 10:00 PT to review results, but we can cancel if you want the pin first.

Thanks 

 Marissa Cole
